claim: Osaka Castle main keep is open daily 9:00–17:00 with last entry 16:30, closed Dec 28–Jan 1, with extended hours to 21:00 during cherry blossom illuminations roughly Mar 20–Apr 12.
quote: The museum operates daily from 9:00–17:00 (last entry 16:30). However, hours extend to 21:00 during the cherry blossom illuminations roughly March 20 – April 12. The castle is closed December 28 – January 1.

claim: The Toyotomi Stone Wall Museum opened April 1, 2025 next to the castle tower, exposing 16th-century Hideyoshi-era walls buried by the Tokugawa after 1615.
quote: The Toyotomi Stone Wall Museum opened its doors on April 1, 2025, nestled right next to the iconic castle tower. The museum exhibits some of the castle's original stone walls, which were covered up by the Tokugawa when they rebuilt the castle after the 1615 battle.

claim: Castle admission is now 1,200 yen (doubled from 600 yen when the Toyotomi Stone Wall Museum opened in April 2025); plan an extra 30–40 minutes to do it justice.
quote: With the opening of the new Toyotomi Stone Wall Museum (in April 2025), they doubled the entrance ticket price to Osaka Castle (from 600 yen to 1200 yen). Plan an extra 30–40 minutes to do it justice.

claim: Best crowd-avoidance window is arriving around 8am to walk the park while it's quiet then enter when the castle opens at 9am, or coming around 4pm; weekdays are quieter than weekends.
quote: arriving around 8am allows you to walk around Osaka Castle Park while it's still quiet and then head inside when the castle opens at 9am. Another good option is coming around 4pm to avoid the biggest crowds in the middle of the day.

claim: Umeda Sky Building Kuchu Teien Observatory is open daily 9:30–22:30 with last admission 22:00 for the period 04/01/2026–03/31/2027; closed Jan 1, 2026; adult admission ¥1,300.
quote: The Umeda Sky Building is open Monday - Sunday from 9:30 AM - 10:30 PM (for the period 04/01/2026 - 03/31/2027). Last admission is at 10:00 PM. Adults: ¥1,300

claim: Shitennoji Temple is one of Japan's oldest Buddhist temples with outer grounds free; inner precinct, Gokuraku-jodo Garden and treasure house require paid admission (~300 yen adult, 200 yen child).
quote: The outer temple grounds are free to enter, but admission to the inner precinct, the Gokuraku-jodo Garden and the treasure house is paid. The fee for adults is 300 yen, while children (elementary and junior high school students) can enter for 200 yen.

claim: Shitennoji opens 8:30 AM with seasonal closing (4:30 PM Apr–Sep, 4:00 PM Oct–Mar); five-storied pagoda can be entered and ascended, and the Main Hall enshrines Prince Shotoku as a Kannon statue.
quote: April - September: 8:30 AM – 4:30 PM and October - March: 8:30 AM – 4:00 PM... a five-storied pagoda that can be entered and ascended and the Main Hall (Kondo) in which Prince Shotoku is enshrined as a statue of Kannon.

claim: Sumiyoshi Taisha is free to enter, open 6:00–17:00 (Apr–Sep) / 6:30–16:30 (Oct–Mar), 3 minutes' walk from Nankai Sumiyoshi-Taisha Station, takes about 45 minutes to one hour to visit.
quote: The shrine is open from 6:00-16:00 (April-September) and 6:30-16:30 (October-March)... From Nankai Main Line, Sumiyoshi-Taisha Station, it's a 3-minute walk... a typical visit takes about 45 minutes to one hour.

claim: Sumiyoshi Taisha's defining feature is the steep vermillion Sorihashi (Taiko/drum) Bridge whose railings reflect in the water to form a circle; best visited early morning around 7:30 on a sunny day for soft light.
quote: the most striking feature in the shrine grounds is the Sorihashi Bridge with its beautiful vermillion railings, also known as 'Taikobashi' (drum bridge)... Highly recommend visiting the shrine at around 7:30 AM on a sunny day.

claim: Tsutenkaku Tower observatory hours from March 1, 2026 are 9:00–22:00, with the Tower Slider (60 m / ~10-second descent from the third floor of the observation deck to basement) running 10:00–20:00.
quote: The new operating hours effective from March 1, 2026 show the Observatory opening from 9:00 AM – 10:00 PM, with the TOWER SLIDER operating from 10:00 AM – 8:00 PM.

claim: Abeno Harukas 300 (Japan's tallest building at 300 m) observation deck spans floors 58–60, open daily 9:00–22:00 with last entry 21:30; adult ticket ¥2,000.
quote: Abeno Harukas Observatory ticket prices vary by age: 2,000 yen for adults... The observatory is open every day from 9.00 – 22.00 with last entry at 21.30... Located on the 58th to 60th floors of the impressive 300-meter-tall Abeno Harukas skyscraper.

claim: Osaka Aquarium Kaiyukan uses dynamic pricing (~¥2,700 adult, ¥1,400 child, ¥700 toddler), typically opens 10:00–20:00 with last admission one hour before close; a full visit takes 2–3 hours.
quote: Ticket prices range from ¥2,700 for adults... The aquarium is open from 10:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m., with last admission one hour before closing... visitors typically spend about 2 to 3 hours exploring thoroughly.

claim: Tempozan Giant Ferris Wheel operates 10:00–22:00 (ticket sales close 15 min before), ¥900 for ages 3+, one revolution takes about 15 minutes with views to Akashi Kaikyo Bridge, Kansai Airport, and the Rokko range on clear days.
quote: Today's operating hours are 10:00～22:00... The standard admission fee is ¥900 per person for visitors aged three and older... The ride takes about 15 minutes, and on a clear day, you can enjoy panoramic views of the Ikoma mountain range to the east, the Akashi Kaikyo Bridge to the west.

claim: Aizuya invented takoyaki in 1935 and serves it sauce-free to highlight dashi batter and octopus; the original shop is in Tamadenishi, about a 10-minute train ride from Namba.
quote: Aizuya is credited with inventing takoyaki back in 1935, and their takoyaki is served without sauce, allowing customers to enjoy the pure flavor of the batter and octopus.

claim: Wanaka's Sennichimae main store sells 8-piece takoyaki for about 650 yen and is known for a crisp-outside, creamy-inside texture.
quote: Wanaka is one of Osaka's most famous takoyaki shops, known for its perfectly balanced texture – crispy on the outside and creamy on the inside ... A standard serving of 8 pieces runs about 650 yen.

claim: Kukuru's Dotonbori store is famous for 'bikkuri takoyaki' with oversized octopus pieces protruding from each ball.
quote: Takoya Dotonbori Kukuru is widely known for its 'bikkuri takoyaki' or 'Surprise Takoyaki.' The surprise element comes from the unusually large pieces of octopus used, with many pieces protruding from the takoyaki balls.

claim: Local consensus picks Kiji, Fukutaro and Mizuno as the top three okonomiyaki shops in Osaka.
quote: The top 3 best okonomiyaki in Osaka are Kiji, Fukutaro, and Mizuno.

claim: Mizuno is a Michelin-listed okonomiyaki shop near Dotonbori with limited seats but a fast-moving queue.
quote: Mizuno is a Michelin star okonomiyaki restaurant that has been awarded 4 consecutive years of Osaka Michelin guide since 2016. The shop is located nearby Dotonbori ... Mizuno is a small restaurant with limited seats. However, the queue moved pretty fast.

claim: Fukutaro in Sennichimae, founded 1945, is a Michelin Bib Gourmand pick famous for its 'Buta-negiyaki' pork-and-green-onion pancake using Kagoshima pork.
quote: Located in the Sennichimae shopping district, 'Fukutaro' is a legendary shop established in 1945 ... Fukutaro is also listed in the Michelin Guide Kyoto/Osaka 2017 Bib Gourmand.

claim: Kushikatsu Daruma sits at the base of Tsutenkaku in Shinsekai; the 16-skewer omakase set is the standard order and double-dipping the communal sauce is forbidden.
quote: Located near the base of Tsutenkaku tower in Shinsekai, Daruma is one of the area's most popular kushikatsu restaurants ... Under no circumstances should you ever double-dip your skewer into the tangy black sauce ... Try the 16-skewer set.

claim: The no-double-dip rule originated at Kushikatsu Daruma and serves both sanitary and cost-control purposes from the dish's working-class origins.
quote: The no double dipping rule is now common sense, but it was Kushikatsu Daruma that established this rule ... the rule also originated from the fact that kushikatsu was initially made to fill up laborers on a budget.

claim: Kuromon Ichiba is a 580m arcade of 150+ shops; authentic stalls are easiest to find on an 8am weekday and roughly 10-15% of vendors close on Sundays.
quote: Authentic stalls are easier to find at 8am on a weekday than at 1pm on a Saturday ... Sundays can be tricky because roughly 10 to 15 percent of vendors close, particularly smaller family-run shops.

claim: Sennichimae Doguyasuji is a 150m kitchenware arcade about five minutes from Kuromon; the two complement each other as food market and tool market.
quote: Sennichimae Doguyasuji is a haven for kitchenware so the two go hand in hand ... Sennichimae Doguyasuji provides an interesting counterpoint to the nearby fresh food market at Kuromon Ichiba.

claim: Hozenji Yokocho is a stone-paved 80m alley two blocks south of Dotonbori with 60+ traditional restaurants and the moss-covered Mizu-kake Fudo shrine, best visited after dark when lanterns are lit.
quote: stone-paved alley, lined with more than 60 traditional and restored shops ... Mizu-kake Fudo, an image of the Buddhist deity Fudo ... Covered in a lush coat of moss ... 3-minute walk from exit 14 of Namba Station.

claim: Inside Hozenji Yokocho, Meoto Zenzai serves the signature sweet red-bean soup, Wasabi does seasonal high-end kushikatsu, and Okazu Izakaya Kuu is a couple-run sake bar suited to bar-hopping.
quote: Okazu Izakaya Kuu, located in the heart of Hozenji Yokocho, is a small shop run by a couple ... Wasabi is a highly recommended spot for those who enjoy high-end kushikatsu ... Meoto Zenzai serves what could be considered Hozenji Yokocho's signature dish: sweet red bean soup.

claim: Locals drink in Tenma (1,000+ bars/restaurants packed in a few blocks) rather than Dotonbori; standing bars charge 30-40% less than seated equivalents.
quote: Tenma is where Osakans go to drink and eat after work ... over 1,000 bars and restaurants crammed into a few square blocks ... Standing bars (tachinomi) charge 30-40% less than seated equivalents.

claim: Sake no Okuda near Temma station is a recommended tachinomi with bar snacks from 50-300 yen and oden/sashimi as the favorites.
quote: Sake no Okuda delivers the authentic experience with beers for sale and bar foods ranging from 50 JPY to 300 JPY—the oden and sashimi are favorites, and it's conveniently located about two minutes from Temma station.

claim: Genroku Sushi pioneered conveyor-belt sushi in Osaka in 1958 and remains a locally popular kaiten-zushi option.
quote: Ganso Mawaru Genroku Zushi is renowned as the pioneer of conveyor belt sushi—in 1958, its founder introduced the innovative 'rotating meal table,' marking the beginning of the conveyor belt sushi phenomenon.

claim: Kitsune udon (udon topped with sweet fried tofu) was invented at Usami-tei Matsubaya in Minami-senba, Osaka, and horumon-yaki built around offal is an Osaka nose-to-tail specialty.
quote: Kitsune udon is udon topped with aburaage ... It originated in Osaka, with the first restaurant to make it being Usami-tei Matsubaya in Minami-senba, Osaka ... In the Osaka dialect, horumon translates to 'discarded goods' so beef or pork offal is the star of the show.

claim: Minami (Namba/Dotonbori/Shinsaibashi/Amerikamura) is one of Osaka's two major city centers with abundant dining and shopping, including Shinsaibashi as the premier shopping arcade and Amerikamura as Osaka's Harajuku-equivalent for youth fashion.
quote: One of Osaka's two major city centers... Shinsaibashi Shopping Arcade is Osaka's premiere shopping center... Amerikamura is Osaka's counterpart to Harajuku, a good place to see the cutting edge of teenage fashion and culture in Japan.

claim: Dotonbori draws millions for its Glico sign, mechanical crab displays and street food, and is equally compelling by day and after dark when neon reflects off the canal; Hozenji Yokocho is two 80m alleys of traditional izakaya reminiscent of Kyoto's Pontocho.
quote: Famous for the iconic Glico Running Man sign, giant mechanical crab displays, and wall-to-wall street food... The area is equally compelling by day and electric after dark, when its neon reflections light up the canal surface.

claim: Grand Front Osaka is a huge two-part shopping mall a 2-minute walk north of JR Osaka Station with 6 floors of fashion/beauty, 3 floors of restaurants, the Knowledge Capital tech showcase, and the Intercontinental Hotel bar for city views.
quote: A huge two-part shopping mall north of JR Osaka Station, Grand Front is one of the best one-stop shopping centers in the city... The core attraction here is 'Knowledge Capital,' where you can check out more shiny, cutting-edge services and products based on newer technological developments.

claim: Nakazakicho, a 10-minute walk from Hankyu Umeda, is a maze of tiny alleys best explored without a map — packed with indie cafes (Taiyo No To, Salon de AManTo), vintage shops and street art, with most spots opening around 11am.
quote: A quaint neighborhood... perfect for frivolous wandering through tiny alleys in search of secluded cafes... It's best to put away the map and follow your instincts.

claim: Tenjinbashi-suji is Japan's longest covered shopping street at 2.5km with over 600 shops — clothes, futons, sundries, tea shops, books, cafes — giving it a significantly more local feel than touristy arcades.
quote: Stretches a whopping 2.5 kilometers long... home to over 600 shops and restaurants... significantly more local feel than its more commercial counterparts.

claim: Shinsekai is a scruffy, deliberately retro 1950s grid beneath Tsutenkaku Tower; the single rule at any kushikatsu joint is no double-dipping the sauce, and the best time to visit is late afternoon from about 16:00 when neon takes over.
quote: It's scruffy, unpretentious, and completely unbothered by the fact that the rest of Osaka has moved on aesthetically... The single non-negotiable rule at any Shinsekai kushikatsu restaurant is no double-dipping... The best time to visit is late afternoon, from around 16:00.

claim: Tsutenkaku Tower (originally 1912, rebuilt 1956) combines Arc de Triomphe and Eiffel Tower design, and Jan Jan Yokocho is a 130m, ~50-shop alley of kushikatsu, doteyaki and shogi clubs that feels like classic downtown Osaka.
quote: Janjan Yokocho, a lively street lined with about 50 shops, including kushikatsu restaurants, doteyaki restaurants, and go and shogi clubs, stretches 130 meters from north to south.

claim: Tennoji is Osaka's third major downtown — anchored by the 300m Abeno Harukas with views as far as Kobe and Wakayama — and pairs naturally with Tennoji Park (zoo, pond, art museum) and a Shinsekai stroll, all walkable.
quote: Osaka's third major downtown hub, Tennoji, is rapidly transforming from a seedy retro wasteland into a happening urban center... The soaring 300-meter-tall Abeno Harukas tower... a fantastic view over the city of Osaka and nearby parts of Kobe, the Inland Sea and Wakayama.

claim: Nakanoshima's eastern half is a roughly 3-hour walking route taking in a waterfront park, the red-brick Central Public Hall (illuminated at night), the Oriental Ceramics museum, the Prefectural Library and the lion-flanked Naniwa Bridge.
quote: A symbol of Osaka's culture, art, and history... lit up at night... Affectionately known as 'Lion Bridge' because of the two stone lions it has.

claim: Nakanoshima Children's Book Forest, designed by Tadao Ando, holds ~20,000 books on wall-to-wall shelves; books can't be borrowed but visitors can take one to read on benches by the river in Nakanoshima Park (9:30-17:00, closed Mondays).
quote: This cultural facility with approximately 20,000 books was designed and built by Tadao Ando... entire walls on the first to third floors being huge bookshelves... many visitors sitting on benches by the river in the park and reading while relaxing.

claim: Den Den Town (Nipponbashi) is Osaka's Akihabara equivalent — electronics, cameras, anime, games — with shops concentrated on Sakaisuji and parallel Ota Road, hosting Mandarake/Animate/Super Potato but with noticeably less foot traffic than Tokyo.
quote: Den-Den Town in Nipponbashi is Osaka's answer to Tokyo's Akihabara... The shops are concentrated along two long, main streets: Nipponbashisuji Shopping Mall on Sakaisuji, and Ota Road which runs parallel... It doesn't see quite the same volume of foot traffic as its Tokyo counterpart.

claim: Karahori Shotengai is an 800m covered street in a pocket of Chuo Ward that escaped WWII air raids, preserving two-story nagaya row houses and narrow roji alleys — quiet, residential, the opposite of Dotonbori and best wandered without a map.
quote: The covered street extends for about 800 meters... a pocket of the city that miraculously sidestepped the devastating air raids of World War II... two-story structures, with their tiled roofs, latticed windows, and shared walls, represent the architectural heartbeat of Karahori.

claim: Amerikamura is Osaka's vintage/streetwear hub a 5-10 minute walk from Shinsaibashi and Namba; the adjacent Horie (Orange Street) is the calmer 'adult' version with curated boutiques, furniture shops and minimalist fashion brands.
quote: Orange Street (Tachibana Dori) in the adjacent Minami Horie area is known for its trendy, independent boutiques and more curated vintage shops... Horie is a ten-minute walk from Amerikamura and is known as the 'adult' version of Amemura.

claim: Nara is reachable from Osaka's Tennoji Station in 30 min for 510 yen via JR Yamatoji Line, or 30 min via Kintetsu limited express from Namba for 1200-1300 yen
quote: The trains stop at Osaka's Tennoji Station (30 minutes, 510 yen one way) when using the JR Yamatoji Line to reach JR Nara Station. By limited express, the one way trip from Osaka-Namba Station to Nara takes about 30 minutes and costs 1200-1300 yen.

claim: A Nara day trip needs at least 6-8 hours on the ground to cover the main sights
quote: Aim for at least 6 to 8 hours on the ground when planning your day trip to make the most of your time in Nara.

claim: Todaiji houses one of Japan's largest bronze Buddha statues (15m tall) and opens 7:30am-5:30pm April-October
quote: The massive building houses one of Japan's largest bronze statues of Buddha (Daibutsu). The 15 meters tall, seated Buddha represents Vairocana. Open from 7:30 am to 5:30 pm during the months of April through October.

claim: Nara Park is a 660-hectare park with ~1200 free-roaming wild deer (a National Natural Monument) and UNESCO sites Todaiji, Kofukuji, Kasuga Taisha
quote: Almost 1200 wild deer roam Nara Park. The deer of Nara Park are a National Natural Monument, and you can feed them with shika senbei sold in the park.

claim: JR Kyoto Line Special Rapid runs Osaka Station to Kyoto in ~30 min for 580 yen with departures every 15 minutes
quote: The JR Kyoto Line Special Rapid runs between Osaka Station and Kyoto Station in about 30 minutes, costs 580 yen one way, and leaves often enough that you do not need military-grade timing. Trains run every 15 minutes.

claim: Tokaido Shinkansen Hikari/Kodama runs Shin-Osaka to Kyoto in 15 min for 1,450 yen unreserved; Hankyu Limited Express runs Osaka-Umeda to central Kyoto in 45 min for 410 yen
quote: JR Tokaido-Sanyo Shinkansen (Hikari/Kodama): 15 min from Shin-Osaka, 1,450 yen unreserved. Hankyu Kyoto Line Limited Express: 45 min from Osaka-Umeda, 410 yen.

claim: Fushimi Inari Shrine features ~1,000 vermilion torii gates and takes 1-2 hours depending on how far up the trail you walk
quote: The shrine is a prominent Shinto shrine famous for its countless vermilion torii gates, with a trail of 1,000 vermilion torii gates creating a magical path. Allow 1-2 hours, depending on how far you walk into the tunnel of gates.

claim: Allow at least 9 hours in Kyoto to do the major sights (Fushimi Inari, Kiyomizu-dera, Arashiyama, Gion) on a one-day trip — travel time is on top of that
quote: Allow at least nine hours in Kyoto to do all of the major sights – travel time to and from your hotel would be on top of that, so expect a long day.

claim: JR Special Rapid runs Osaka to Kobe-Sannomiya in 20 min for 420 yen; Hankyu Limited Express runs Osaka-Umeda to Kobe-Sannomiya in 25 min for 330 yen
quote: JR special rapid trains require 20 minutes and cost 420 yen for the one way trip from Osaka Station to Kobe's Sannomiya Station. Alternatively, limited express trains on the Hankyu Kobe Line take 25 minutes and cost 330 yen from Osaka-Umeda Station to Kobe-Sannomiya Station.

claim: Mt. Rokko in Kobe is reached by Hankyu to Rokko Station then bus #16 to cablecar (15+14+10 min, ~1,010 yen one-way) for panoramic views as far as Osaka
quote: Take Hankyu Railway from Sannomiya Station to Rokko Station (15 minutes, 200 yen). Then Kobe City Bus #16 to Rokko Cablecar (14 minutes, 210 yen). Then Rokko Cablecar up Mount Rokko (10 minutes; 600 yen one-way). On a clear day, you can see as far as Osaka.

claim: Kobe's Kitano Ijinkan district is a 19th-century foreign settlement of Western-style mansions at the foot of Mt. Rokko, alongside Kobe beef as the city's signature experiences
quote: Kobe Kitano Ijinkan is a district, located at the foot of Rokkosan, where in the 19th century a number of western-style designed buildings and residences were constructed. These mansions (Ijikan), were used as residences for diplomats and international merchants.

claim: Sanyo Shinkansen from Shin-Osaka reaches Himeji in 30 min; the castle is a 15-minute walk from the station; budget 3-4 hours for castle + Kokoen Garden
quote: The shinkansen from Shin-Osaka takes 30 minutes, and the main gate is a flat 15-minute walk from the station. Budget three to four hours for the castle and Kokoen Garden, grab lunch nearby, and you're back in Osaka for dinner.

claim: Himeji Castle admission rises to 2,500 yen for non-resident adults from March 2026; Shinkansen one-way Shin-Osaka to Himeji costs ~2,980 yen non-reserved
quote: Himeji Castle (non-residents, adults, from March 2026): 2,500 yen. Round-trip by JR Sanyo Shinkansen (Hikari/Kodama) from Shin-Osaka: approximately 5,960 yen.

claim: Koyasan is reached via Nankai Koya Line from Namba: limited express to Gokurakubashi takes 80 min (1,880 yen e-ticket), then 5-min cablecar (500 yen) and 10-min bus into town — about 2 hours total each way
quote: Limited express trains operate directly to Gokurakubashi (80 minutes, 1880 yen for an e-ticket, 2 trains/day). From Gokurakubashi, transfer to the cablecar which travels up the mountain to Koyasan taking about five minutes and costing 500 yen. From the top station, it is a ten minute bus ride into the town center.

claim: Nankai's new GRAN Tenku luxury sightseeing train begins service April 24, 2026 between Namba and Gokurakubashi, with a ~90-minute scenic journey
quote: Nankai Electric Railway's new sightseeing train, the GRAN Tenku, will begin service on April 24, 2026, operating between Namba Station in Osaka and Gokurakubashi Station. The approximately 90-minute journey.

claim: For short Kansai trips the most economical strategy is ICOCA pay-as-you-go for intra-region travel, reserving the JR Pass only for long-distance use
quote: The most economical and comfortable strategy is to use the ICOCA IC card as your main method, and use the Japan Rail Pass only for long-distance travel.

claim: A nationwide JR Pass is not worth it for a short Kansai-only trip — short hops like Osaka-Kyoto are 400-600 yen and ICOCA pay-as-you-go beats any unlimited pass
quote: For short-distance travel, such as between Osaka and Kyoto (about 400–600 yen), it is more economical to pay as you go with ICOCA rather than using an expensive unlimited ride pass.

claim: USJ is a full-day in-city alternative; from March 4, 2026 the park runs its 25th Anniversary celebrations alongside Universal Cool Japan 2026 with Detective Conan, Jujutsu Kaisen and Frieren attractions
quote: From March 4, 2026, USJ begins its 25th Anniversary celebrations, alongside Universal Cool Japan 2026, featuring limited-time attractions based on Detective Conan, Jujutsu Kaisen, and Frieren.

claim: USJ uses dynamic ticket pricing and tickets release 60 days before visit date; Express Pass 7 is the safest add-on for covering Super Nintendo World and main rides in one day
quote: Universal Studios Japan tickets can be booked up to 2 months in advance, with tickets going on sale 60 days in advance. Universal Studios Japan operates dynamic ticket pricing. If you want to enjoy Super Nintendo World and the main rides in one day without early gate sprints, Express Pass 7 is the safest choice.

claim: Expo 2025 Osaka Kansai closed on October 13, 2025 after 184 days and 28 million visitors — it is not a 2026 attraction
quote: Expo 2025 was open for six months, from 13 April to 13 October 2025. The Expo welcomed over 28 million visitors during its six-month run.

claim: USJ Express Passes are released exactly 60 days before visit date and frequently sell out for weekends; Express Pass 7 is the balanced choice covering Super Nintendo World's high-demand rides.
quote: Express passes for Universal Studios Japan are available exactly 60 days in advance – at midnight... Popular Express Passes often sell out in advance, especially for weekends and holiday periods.

claim: Donkey Kong Country officially opened at USJ Super Nintendo World on December 11, 2024, expanding the area by 70% with the Mine-Cart Madness coaster.
quote: World's First Area Featuring Donkey Kong 'DONKEY KONG COUNTRY' Officially Opens on December 11, 2024... SUPER NINTENDO WORLD expanded by 70% its current size with an all-new area.

claim: Entry to Super Nintendo World requires an Area Timed Entry Ticket, Standby Entry Ticket, or Express Pass with advance Area Timed Entry booking; same-day distribution may run out early.
quote: To enter SUPER NINTENDO WORLD, an 'Universal Express Pass with an Area Timed Entry Ticket: Advance Booking' or 'Area Timed Entry Ticket'/'Standby Entry Ticket' is required.

claim: teamLab Botanical Garden Osaka is located inside Nagai Botanical Garden in Higashisumiyoshi Ward, opens after sunset, adult tickets from 1,800 yen, closed 2nd and 4th Mondays.
quote: Nagai Botanical Garden, 1-23 Nagai Park, Higashisumiyoshi Ward, Osaka City... Adults (high school and above): from ¥1,800... closes on the 2nd and 4th Mondays monthly.

claim: From June 1 to July 31, 2026, teamLab Botanical Garden Osaka operates 19:45–21:30 with last entry 20:30; tickets are sold online only.
quote: From June 1 to July 31, 2026, the garden operates from 19:45 - 21:30 with last entry at 20:30... Tickets are only sold online.

claim: Hanshin Tigers have nine home games at Koshien in June 2026 (vs Seibu Jun 2-4, Rakuten Jun 5-7, Yakult Jun 23-25, Chunichi Jun 30); official tickets run 3,000–6,000 yen, resellers charge 30,000–88,000 yen.
quote: Price Range: ¥3,000–¥6,000 through official channels; resellers charge ¥30,000–¥88,000... vs Tohoku Rakuten Golden Eagles (June 5–7): Friday, June 5: 18:00 first pitch; Saturday, June 6: 14:00 first pitch.

claim: Grand sumo tournaments occur only in odd-numbered months (Jan, Mar, May, Jul, Sep, Nov); there is no honbasho in June 2026, and the May basho is in Tokyo with the next being July in Nagoya at the new IG Arena.
quote: Grand tournaments (honbasho) are held in January, March, May, July, September, and November... The July Nagoya Basho marks the debut of the new IG Arena.

claim: The June 2026 Bunraku Wakate-kai (young performers') showcase runs only Saturday June 20 and Sunday June 21 at the National Bunraku Theatre Osaka, tickets 3,300 yen (student 2,300), advance sales open May 18, 2026.
quote: Performance Dates: Saturday, June 20 – Sunday, June 21, 2026... Ticket Pricing: 3,300yen (Student 2,300yen)... Advance booking opens at 10:00 on Monday, May 18, 2026.

claim: Nakanoshima Museum of Art Osaka runs two notable exhibitions in June 2026: Takashima Yajuro 50th Anniversary retrospective (Mar 25–Jun 21) and Enfants Terribles featuring Morimura, Yanobe, Yanagi (Apr 25–Jul 20).
quote: The '50th Anniversary of Takashima Yajuro's Passing' exhibition will be held from March 25 (Wed) to June 21 (Sun), 2026... Enfants Terribles, Premonitions of Oblivion by Morimura Yasumasa, Yanobe Kenji, and Yanagi Miwa runs from April 25 – July 20, 2026.

claim: June 2026 fireworks events near Osaka include Rinku Fireworks Festival (Sat Jun 6, Marble Beach) and Japan Fireworks Expo 2026 restaging the Expo finale on Sun Jun 7 at Yumeshima.
quote: Rinku Fireworks Festival will be returning for its 10th year in 2026, held at Rinku Park's Marble Beach on Saturday June 6, with a 40-minute display featuring 7,000 fireworks... The grand fireworks from last year's Osaka Expo will be restaged on Sunday June 7.

claim: Osaka's 2026 tsuyu rainy season is forecast to start June 6 and end July 19, putting the trip squarely inside it.
quote: Osaka shares almost identical rainy season dates with Kyoto... The predicted start is June 6, 2026, and the predicted end is July 19, 2026.

claim: More than half of June in Osaka typically sees rain with temps 20-27C; early/mid-June is drier than late June.
quote: More than half of June typically experiences rainfall... Traveling in early to mid-June is preferable to late June as rainfall tends to increase and lasts longer later in the month.

claim: Osaka Amazing Pass for 2026 runs 3,500 yen for 1-day and 5,000 yen for 2-day, covers ~40 attractions plus Metro/bus/private rail.
quote: The 1-day pass costs ¥3,500 and the 2-day pass costs ¥5,000... unlimited rides on Osaka Metro, city buses, the New Tram, and several private railway lines.

claim: The Amazing Pass is now digital-only (QR code) since June 2024 and includes Umeda Sky Building, Tombori River Cruise, and Osaka Castle Museum admission.
quote: The pass is now available only as a digital QR-code ticket, since the physical card version ended in June 2024.

claim: Kansai Railway Pass Lite (formerly Kansai Thru Pass) is 5,600 yen for 2 days or 7,000 yen for 3 days but excludes JR trains and Kyoto subway — overkill for a city-only weekend.
quote: A two-day pass costs 5,600 JPY, while a three-day pass costs 7,000 JPY... unlimited use of trains in the Kansai Region around Osaka with the prominent exception of JR trains and Kyoto subways.

claim: Osaka Metro's Enjoy Eco 1-day pass is just 620 yen on weekends/holidays vs 820 yen weekdays — the cheapest pure transit option for a Saturday/Sunday.
quote: The Enjoy Eco Card costs 820 yen for adults on weekdays and 620 yen on weekends and holidays.

claim: Saturday is the single busiest USJ day with ~52-minute average waits, so locate USJ on Sunday or skip during a weekend trip.
quote: The busiest day to visit Universal Studios Japan is Saturday with a 52 minute average wait time.

claim: Hajime (3-star) reservations open exactly two months ahead and require reconfirmation 1-2 weeks before; dress code is business casual with jackets and leather shoes for men, no jeans/shorts/sneakers.
quote: Reservations at Hajime become available two months to the date in advance, and must be reconfirmed between one and two weeks prior to avoid a cancellation.

claim: Fujiya 1935 (Michelin 2-star in 2026 guide) publishes formal house rules covering attire and cancellation, indicating high-end Osaka kaiseki/innovative venues all enforce smart-casual minimums.
quote: Fujiya 1935 is a Two Stars restaurant in the 2026 MICHELIN Guide Japan.

claim: Official Osaka tourism board confirms covered arcades Shinsaibashi, Tenjinbashisuji (2.6 km, longest in Japan) and Dotonbori as rainy-day fallback corridors.
quote: Osaka's covered shopping arcades — Shinsaibashi, Tenjinbashisuji, Dotonbori — make it especially navigable on rainy days, with Tenjinbashisuji being the longest covered shopping arcade in Japan at 2.6 km.
